$comment: BRIEF.md §10: 'Products, prices, durations, coverage and depth in one data file.
The coverage × depth grid renders from it, including the not offered cells.'
The grid is rendered twice — home and services — and the two hand-authored copies
in the handover had drifted by one cell (see CHANGES.md #3). One record now feeds
both, which is the only way they stay identical.
`notOffered` cells are data, not absence. RATIONALE.md: absence is always labelled
and always legible, and that includes the commercial ladder.
An amount is a NUMBER here, and carries no currency symbol, no thousands comma,
no `from`, no `/month` and no VAT suffix. Every one of those is a rendering
decision, and all of them now live in the `price` filter in eleventy.config.js.
That is not tidiness. Until 2026-08-11 these fields held display strings with the
symbol, the comma, the floor and the period all baked in, and the consequence was
that adding a VAT suffix meant editing twenty rendered strings by hand — a set with
no membership rule, so the next price somebody adds is added without the suffix and
nothing notices. `from` and `period` are structured here so that the suffix ORDER is
a property of the code: the period binds to the amount and VAT comes last, never the
other way round. Check 26 keeps the symbol out of this file and every other one.
`from` marks a floor. `period` marks a recurring charge. Absent means neither.
